<a name="claude-mem"></a>
### 🥇 [claude-mem](https://github.com/thedotmack/claude-mem) <sub>score [97](../README.md#-how-we-rank "Score 97/100. Adoption: widely used (98) · Freshness: active (100) · Maintenance: healthy (97) · Agent-ready: ready (85) (each out of 100, weighted). Click for how we rank.") · ⭐ 120k · Apache-2.0 · Nov 2026</sub>

**Persistent cross-session memory plugin for Claude Code and other coding agents.**

Claude-mem hooks into Claude Code's lifecycle events (SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse, PostToolUse, Stop, SessionEnd) to capture tool-usage observations, summarize them, and inject relevant context into later sessions. Data is stored in SQLite with FTS5 and Chroma for hybrid search, served by a local Bun-managed worker with a web viewer. Search is exposed through three MCP tools (search, timeline, get_observations). Installers also exist for OpenCode, T3 Code, Antigravity, OMP, Pi and OpenClaw.

- **+** Local SQLite plus Chroma storage with a worker HTTP API and web viewer
- **+** Three-step search/timeline/get_observations flow filters before fetching full details, cutting tokens
- **+** Installers for several harnesses besides Claude Code, including OpenCode, T3 Code and OpenClaw
- **+** `<private>` tags exclude sensitive content from storage
- **−** Installer prompts for sign-in to a hosted observer with a 30-day trial; opt-out needs flags
- **−** Depends on Node 20+, Bun and uv, auto-installed if missing
- **−** `npm install -g claude-mem` gives only the SDK, not the hooks or worker
- **−** Some features, such as TeamBrain and cloud sync, rely on the hosted cmem.ai service

<sub>no GPU · Docker + Compose · Needs Node.js >=20, Bun, uv, SQLite, Chroma · Models: Anthropic plan, OpenRouter, Gemini, claude-mem observer · safety checks passed 10 of 11 · [Repo](https://github.com/thedotmack/claude-mem) · [📖 Docs ↗](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/) · [🌐 Site ↗](https://cmem.ai) · [📊 Score breakdown ↗](https://archestack.com/best-of-vibe-coding/projects/claude-mem/)</sub>

**Markdown slash-command skills that give Claude Code planning, review, QA and ship roles.**

gstack is a set of Markdown skills, exposed as slash commands such as /office-hours, /plan-ceo-review, /review, /qa, /cso and /ship, that split a coding session into roles: product, architecture, design, review, QA, security and release. Setup is a git clone into ~/.claude/skills plus a Bun-based ./setup script that also builds a bundled browser for QA. Claude Code is the full-tier host; Codex, OpenCode, Cursor, Kiro and others are experimental.

- **+** Claude Code is the only full-tier host; safety hooks like /careful and /freeze are enforced there
- **+** Skills are plain Markdown, so they can be forked and edited
- **+** Team mode auto-updates for shared repos with no vendored files
- **+** Installs for multiple agents (Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, Kiro, Copilot CLI) via --host flags
- **−** Non-Claude hosts are experimental or instruction-only, and safety skills only advise there
- **−** Outside reviews need a second CLI (Codex or Claude Code) installed and signed in
- **−** /cso needs a recent Bun with specific build flags plus a native C toolchain
- **−** README leads with the author's productivity claims, not behavior of the skills

**Shortens coding-agent replies and compresses tool output before the model reads it.**

Caveman installs through an npx CLI, plugin or skill for Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, OpenCode and 30+ other agents. It makes replies terse while keeping code and paths verbatim, and shrinks logs, JSON, CSV and test output before the model reads them. It also has an Auto model router and reusable script blocks. The README reports 33.2% fewer input tokens over 54 Claude Code runs.

- **+** One npx command detects and configures 30+ agents
- **+** README lists losing cases: HTML 9.9% worse, grep-defs loses to bare grep
- **+** Never rewrites the user's prompt; code, commands and paths stay verbatim
- **+** Voice skill can be installed alone with npx skills add, no proxy
- **−** Auto routing needs a free account; its benchmark is half done and interim
- **−** Output saving over a 'be concise' prompt is about 3% at median
- **−** No HTML compressor yet; session benchmark ran on an older engine
- **−** Per-request billing such as GitHub Copilot gains nothing from shorter answers

<sub>no GPU · Docker + Compose · Needs Node.js 22.13+, A supported coding agent (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, etc.) · Models: Claude, OpenAI, Gemini CLI agents, open models via Auto · safety checks passed 10 of 12 · [Repo](https://github.com/juliusbrussee/caveman) · [▶️ Demo ↗](https://caveman.so/demo) · [📖 Docs ↗](https://docs.caveman.so) · [🌐 Site ↗](https://caveman.so) · [📊 Score breakdown ↗](https://archestack.com/best-of-vibe-coding/projects/caveman/)</sub>

TokenEconomizer is a plugin for Claude Code, Codex, GitHub Copilot CLI and Pi, with experimental support for several other agents. It learns from past sessions in a repository and applies three mechanisms: micro-skills (repeated facts injected at session start), tool pruning (unused tools left out via agent settings) and a loop guard that redirects stuck turns. The authors report 18.4–30.9% lower mean cost on SWE-Bench tasks across five agent–model combinations.

**Pre-execution hook that blocks destructive commands and secret access by coding agents.**

CC Safety Net installs as a hook in coding agent CLIs and parses each shell command or file access before it runs. It blocks things like `git reset --hard`, `git push --force`, `rm -rf` on dangerous targets, `curl | bash`, and reads of SSH keys, `.env` files and `~/.aws`, including when wrapped in `bash -c` or `python -c`. It is not a sandbox and does not restrict processes, filesystem permissions or network egress.

- **+** Supports 16 coding CLIs, including Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and Gemini CLI, on Windows, macOS, Linux
- **+** Parses command semantics, so wrapping in bash -c or reordering flags does not bypass rules
- **+** Standard, Strict and Paranoid presets, a GUI editor, and rulebooks for Terraform, AWS, gcloud, Azure
- **+** Policy lives in a committed .cc-safety-net/ directory; a broken config never blocks commands
- **−** Not a sandbox: no process containment, filesystem permissions or network egress monitoring
- **−** Requires Node.js 18 or higher
- **−** Must keep the @latest qualifier on npx, or a stale cached copy may run

- **+** Detects 18 LLM providers and 10 frameworks, including LangGraph, CrewAI and LlamaIndex
- **+** Graph nodes link to the exact function and line; export to PNG supported

- **+** Registers an MCP server automatically in .cursor/mcp.json or .mcp.json
- **−** Initial analysis needs a self-hosted backend and a Gemini API key
- **−** Hosted backend is only a roadmap item
- **−** Cursor needs a manual .vsix build and install

The CLI prints readable tables in a terminal and a JSON envelope with next_actions when piped.

- **+** Three discovery paths: docs parsing, active probing, and peek-api captures
- **+** Generated client includes auth, pagination, retry with backoff, rate limiting, and caching
- **+** Shows the endpoint catalog for review before generating any code
- **−** Requires Claude Code; not usable as a standalone tool
- **−** Generated CLI is TypeScript run via npx tsx, so a Node toolchain is needed
- **−** Install is a manual copy of the skill/ folder; no package or installer

**Claude skill that polls ChatGPT and Gemini, then merges their advice into one plan.**

A Claude skill that, on prompts like "consult the council", sends the question to OpenAI and Gemini through a Python script (scripts/query_llms.py). Claude then compares both answers and presents a merged implementation plan with attribution to each model. Models are set with OPENAI_MODEL and GEMINI_MODEL in a .env file; defaults are gpt-5-nano and gemini-3-flash-preview.

- **+** Model choice per provider is a two-line .env change
- **+** Continues with one model's answer if the other API fails
- **+** Small footprint: one SKILL.md and one Python script
- **+** Final plan attributes ideas to each model
- **−** Limited to two fixed providers, OpenAI and Gemini
- **−** Requires paid API keys for both OpenAI and Google
- **−** Fixed 30-second timeout per API call
- **−** No tagged release; installed by uploading a .skill file
